name: Donkey Calf Raise
description: The donkey calf raise is performed with the torso bent forward at approximately 90° with the hips flexed, which places the gastrocnemius under a greater stretch at the hip than a standing calf raise. Because the gastrocnemius is a biarticular muscle crossing both the knee and hip, the hip-flexed position elongates it, increasing the range of motion and stretch on the gastrocnemius medial and lateral heads. It was popularized as a mass-building calf exercise and can be loaded by having a training partner sit on the hips.

execution.starting_position: Hinge at the hips and brace the hands on a bench, barbell, or wall at hip height. Keep the knees very slightly bent. Stand with the balls of the feet on a raised surface (step edge or plate).
execution.setup_instructions: Place the toes on a step edge or plate so the heels can drop below the platform for full stretch. Hinge the torso to 90° — this is essential for the elongated gastrocnemius position.
steps: Step 1: Position the toes on the edge of a raised surface. Hinge the torso forward 90° and hold onto a support.
Step 2: Lower the heels as far below the step as range of motion allows — full gastrocnemius stretch.
Step 3: Rise onto the toes as high as possible, fully plantar-flexing both ankles.
Step 4: Hold the peak contraction briefly with the calves fully contracted.
Step 5: Lower under control to the stretched position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you rise onto the toes. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Performing with an upright torso, which removes the gastrocnemius pre-stretch benefit
Insufficient heel drop at the bottom — reduces the range of motion
Bouncing through the bottom position — slow the eccentric
safety_considerations: If a partner is adding load by sitting on the hips, communication is essential
Start with bodyweight to establish the movement pattern
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full heel drop below the platform at the bottom; maximum plantar-flexion at the top.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-1-3-0 — slow controlled descent (3s) to maximize gastrocnemius stretch
coaching_cues: Drop the heels all the way — don't cheat the stretch
Rise all the way onto the big toe
Hips bent 90° — don't stand up during the exercise
